l1: What is the exact error code shown in Windows Update?
Is the failure tied to a specific KB number, such as KB5012639?
Is the device managed by WSUS, Intune, or Windows Update for Business?
Is the issue affecting one device or multiple devices in the environment?
Is this environment using Windows Update for Business (WUfB) deferral/dual-scan policies alongside WSUS or SCCM?
Is the issue related to a cumulative update (LCU), servicing stack update (SSU), or component store?
What is the KB number and exact HRESULT/error code of the failing update?
Which servicing channel is targeted — Semi-Annual Channel (SAC) or Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC)?
Is this a single device issue or seen across multiple devices on the same build?
l2: What update ring or deferral policy is applied via Intune or GPO?
Does CBS.log show a CSI failure such as ERROR_SXS_ASSEMBLY_MISSING or ERROR_SXS_COMPONENT_STORE_CORRUPT?
Has the device recently undergone a hardware or firmware change?
Is the WSUS server healthy and reachable from this client?
Is Dual Scan occurring — is the client scanning against both Windows Update/Microsoft Update AND the WSUS/SCCM server on the same scheduled interval?
Is the servicing stack update (SSU) installed and current for this build?
Does CBS.log show a CSI-layer failure (look for the last (F) line and its HRESULT)?
Is there a pending.xml or PendingFileRenameOperations blocking further servicing?
Is the device using a custom WIM image with slipstreamed updates?
Has the System Update Readiness Tool (CheckSUR) been run on this build, and does checksur.log show any 'Unavailable repair files' entries?

l1: Run 'winver' to confirm current build and version.
Check Settings > Windows Update > Update history for failed entries.
Run 'Get-WindowsUpdateLog' to generate a readable WindowsUpdate.log from the ETW trace in C:\Windows\Logs\WindowsUpdate.
Run 'sc query wuauserv' to confirm the Update service is running.
Run 'Get-HotFix' to list currently installed updates.
Run 'DISM /Online /Get-Packages' to review installed servicing packages.
Check Event Viewer > Setup for Event ID 3 (Microsoft-Windows-Servicing) package failures.
Confirm the servicing stack update version with 'DISM /Online /Get-CurrentEdition'.
l2: Review UpdateSessionOrchestration.etl in C:\ProgramData\USOShared\Logs to see whether download, install, or commit is stalling.
Check NotificationUxBroker.etl in the same USOShared\Logs folder to confirm whether reboot/availability toasts fired.
Search CBS.log for the last (F) failure line and note the HRESULT and Facility=FACILITY_WIN32 code shown.
Run 'DISM /Online /Get-Packages' and compare the KB's package state against a known-good baseline.

Know the servicing component roles when reading logs: CSI makes the actual file/registry changes, CBS is the orchestrator, DMI handles advanced driver installation, SMI manages registry settings, DPX decompresses packages, and SQM is just reporting telemetry (usually ignorable).

If a CBS.log failure location is unclear (file vs registry), run it under Process Monitor and use Tools > Count Occurrences on the Result column, filtering for 'not found', 'access denied', or 'sharing violation' to pinpoint the exact failing operation.
In CBS.log, trace backward from the last (F) failure line to find the originating HRESULT/NTSTATUS and its Facility=FACILITY_WIN32 code (look it up in winerror.h).
Run 'Get-PendingReboot' (or check for C:\Windows\WinSXS\pending.xml) to determine which reboot-pending category is active: CBServicing, WindowsUpdate, PendFileRename, or PendComputerRename.
Run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore' for store health and size.
Compare installed package versions against the known-good baseline for the build using 'DISM /Online /Get-Packages'.
Walk the CBS.log transaction workflow in order — Planning, Resolving, Staging, Install/Uninstall, Completion, then Reboot Required — to find exactly which stage the failure occurred in.
Review checksur.log under C:\Windows\Logs\CBS for 'Unavailable repair files:' entries — these name the specific corrupted files that DISM /RestoreHealth could not repair from local sources.

Confirm the exact enforced policy under 'Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update > Windows Update for Business' by reading the registry directly at HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate — check BranchReadinessLevel (e.g. 4 = Preview Build - Slow, 16 = Semi-Annual Channel) and DeferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays (max 365).
Use an RFL (Recommended Fix List) SDP report to identify whether newer versions exist for the specific binaries being updated, when it's unclear if the installed files are already current.
Use 'Spyman' (or simply 'expand' the .msu first) to inspect exactly which .cab payloads and files are bundled inside an update package before assuming a file is missing.
Search C:\Windows\Logs\CBS and related setup log folders for the literal string ', error' across all files/subfolders to quickly shortlist which log files actually contain an error worth opening.

l1: Restart the Windows Update service and BITS service.
Run the built-in Windows Update Troubleshooter.
Clear the SoftwareDistribution folder and retry the update.
Check available disk space on the system drive.
Retry the update after a clean reboot to clear pending operations.
Manually download and install the update package from the Update Catalog.
Run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup' to reduce store size.
Confirm sufficient disk space before reattempting the servicing operation.
Run 'wuauclt /detectnow' (or trigger a scan via Settings) to force an immediate detection cycle instead of waiting for the schedule.
Rename both SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 (after stopping wuauserv, bits, and cryptsvc) if updates neither download nor recognize as already installed.
l2: For a missing/corrupt package (e.g. 0x800F0831), manually expand the .msu with 'expand -F:* KB.msu C:\test\temp' and add the extracted .cab with 'DISM /Online /Add-Package /PackagePath:<cab>'.

For ERROR_SXS_ASSEMBLY_MISSING (0x80073701), download the KB that owns the missing assembly and either add or remove it offline with 'DISM /online /add-package' or '/remove-package' pointed at the extracted .cab.

For ERROR_SXS_COMPONENT_STORE_CORRUPT (0x80073712), load the COMPONENTS hive offline, locate the component under DerivedData\Components, compare its CanonicalData\Deployments key against a healthy machine, merge the missing binary value, then run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'.
Run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth then SFC /scannow for general component store corruption.

For a suspected Dual Scan issue, confirm the 'DisableDualScan' policy state and check for a $MUSM = New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.ServiceManager script result to see which update services are actually registered on the client.

For a stuck CBServicing pending reboot: boot to WinRE and run 'Dism /image:C:\ /cleanup-image /revertpendingactions', or back up and delete the PendingXMLidentifier / AdvancedInstallerNeedResolving keys under HKLM\COMPONENTS.

For installer rollback CBS_E_INSTALLERS_FAILED (0x800f0922) caused by 0KB token files: check C:\Windows\system32\spp\tokens\skus\<edition>\ for zero-byte files, compare against a healthy machine, and delete the invalid ones before retrying.

For ERROR_SXS_COMPONENT_STORE_CORRUPT (0x80073712): load the offline COMPONENTS hive, compare the failing component's CanonicalData\Deployments key against a healthy machine, merge the missing value, then run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'.
For a disk-full rollback (ERROR_DISK_FULL during BFSVC install): free system-drive space and retry; this surfaces as 0x800f0922 with a Boot File Servicing installer failure in CBS.log.

If checksur.log lists 'Unavailable repair files', manually source and place those exact files in the correct packages folder, or supply a known-good source with 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:<path>'.

For pre-Windows 10/Server 2016 systems, run the appropriate System Update Readiness Tool (standalone download for Windows Server 2008/2008 R2) before DISM-based repair, since older builds don't have CheckSUR built in — then follow the same checksur.log 'Unavailable repair files' remediation.

For Windows 7/Server 2008(R2) specifically, run the version-specific standalone System Update Readiness Tool (Windows 7, Server 2008 R2, or Server 2008 SP2 each have their own download) before attempting DISM-based repair, since CheckSUR isn't built in on those OSes.
Confirm the latest Servicing Stack Update (SSU) is installed before troubleshooting further — an outdated SSU is a common root cause of otherwise-unexplained update failures.
For a stuck pending-reboot/component state, the precise recovery command is 'dism /image:c:\ /cleanup-image /revertpendingactions /scratchdir:c:\temp' run from WinRE against the offline OS volume.
As a last-resort manual collection when tooling isn't available, gather C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution directly alongside CBS.log for offline analysis.

l1: Export Settings > Windows Update > Update history as a screenshot.
Collect the exact error code and correlation ID from the UI.
Note the device's current OS build number from winver.
Record whether the device is on Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or VPN during install.
Record the KB number and exact error code for the failed update.
Note the current build number and servicing channel in use.
Confirm free disk space at the time of the failed installation.
Note whether the failure is reproducible on other devices of the same build.
l2: Collect CBS.log and DISM.log from Windows\Logs\CBS and Windows\Logs\DISM.
Run Get-WindowsUpdateLog and capture the merged WindowsUpdate.log file.
Collect UpdateSessionOrchestration.etl and NotificationUxBroker.etl from C:\ProgramData\USOShared\Logs.
If a CSI error is present, export the COMPONENTS registry hive for offline comparison against a healthy device.
Collect CBS.log and DISM.log from Windows\Logs\CBS and Windows\Logs\DISM (and any CbsPersist_*.log/.cab archives).
Collect the Setup Event Log entry for Event ID 3 (Microsoft-Windows-Servicing) with its exact package name and status code.
Collect 'Get-PendingReboot' output or confirm presence of C:\Windows\WinSXS\pending.xml.
If component store corruption is suspected, export the relevant DerivedData\Components and CanonicalData\Deployments registry keys.

If driver updates are bundled with the package, also check the DOQ (Driver Update Queue) staging/install entries and the Critical Driver installation block in CBS.log, which run after the main package install.

Collect a Windows Setup Diagnostic Package (SDCON) where possible — it gathers most of what's needed for update/servicing escalations in one pass (not supported on Server Core), alongside the Server Manager log and ServerManagerInstallationLog.html under C:\Windows\Logs for pre-2012 role/feature installs.

steps.action: Search CBS.log for 'Failed to pin deployment' with HRESULT 0x80073701
steps.expect: Log names the specific package (e.g. Package_2_for_KBxxxx) that is missing

steps.action: Identify the KB that owns the missing assembly referenced in the log
steps.expect: A specific KB number is confirmed as the source of the missing component

steps.action: Download and extract that KB, then run 'DISM /online /add-package /packagepath:<cab>'
steps.expect: Package installs and the missing assembly is restored

steps.action: If add-package fails, extract the KB and run 'DISM /online /remove-package /packagepath:<cab>' instead to clear the stale reference
steps.expect: The stale reference is removed without error

steps.action: Retry the original failing update
steps.expect: Update installs without rolling back

steps.action: Search CBS.log for 'Failed to EnumerateComponentDeployment' with HRESULT 0x80073712
steps.expect: Log names the specific corrupted component

steps.action: Load the offline COMPONENTS hive (File > Load Hive on HKLM, pointing at C:\Windows\System32\Config\COMPONENTS)
steps.expect: Hive loads under a temporary key such as HKLM\Test

steps.action: Navigate to Test\DerivedData\Components and locate the failing component name
steps.expect: The component's registry key is found and inspected

steps.action: Compare the matching key under Test\CanonicalData\Deployments against a healthy reference machine
steps.expect: A missing REG_BINARY value (e.g. appid) is identified

steps.action: Export the key from the healthy machine and merge it into the broken machine's registry, then unload the hive
steps.expect: Key merges without error

steps.action: Run 'DISM /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth'
steps.expect: Component store repair completes successfully

steps.action: Retry installing the originally failing update
steps.expect: Update installs successfully

kb_missing_or_corrupt_0x800f0831.title: Update fails with 0x800F0831 — target package missing or corrupted

steps.action: Check CBS.log for the KB named in the failure (e.g. KB5012639)
steps.expect: CBS.log confirms that specific package is missing or corrupted

steps.action: Manually download the failing KB's .msu package
steps.expect: Package downloads successfully from the Update Catalog

steps.action: Extract it with 'expand -F:* C:\test\KBxxxx.msu C:\test\temp'
steps.expect: A Windows-KBxxxx.cab file appears in C:\test\temp

steps.action: Install it with 'DISM /Online /Add-Package /PackagePath:C:\test\temp\Windows-KBxxxx.cab'
steps.expect: DISM reports the operation completed successfully

steps.action: Retry Windows Update
steps.expect: The update installs without the 0x800F0831 error

dual_scan_conflicts_with_wsus.title: Client dual-scans against both Windows Update and WSUS/SCCM

steps.action: In WindowsUpdate.log (via Get-WindowsUpdateLog), confirm a scan is firing against both Windows/Microsoft Update and the WSUS/SCCM server on the same schedule
steps.expect: Confirms dual scan is actually occurring, not just suspected

steps.action: Run '$MUSM = New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.ServiceManager' then inspect its registered Services collection in PowerShell
steps.expect: Shows exactly which update services (WU, WSUS, etc.) are registered on the client

steps.action: Set the 'Do not allow update deferral policies to cause scans against Windows Update' (DisableDualScan) policy as intended for this environment
steps.expect: Client scans only against the intended source (WSUS/SCCM or Windows Update, not both)

steps.action: Re-check WindowsUpdate.log on the next scheduled scan
steps.expect: Only one scan source fires as expected

cumulative_update_fails_to_install.title: Cumulative update repeatedly fails to install

steps.action: Confirm the exact KB number and error code from Update history
steps.expect: Failure details are captured accurately

steps.action: Review CBS.log around the timestamp of the failed install
steps.expect: Identifies the specific failing component or package

steps.action: Run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
steps.expect: Component store repair completes successfully

steps.action: Retry the cumulative update installation
steps.expect: Update installs without the prior error

steps.action: Run 'Get-HotFix' to confirm the KB is now listed as installed
steps.expect: KB appears in the installed updates list

installer_rollback_cbs_e_installers_fail.title: Patch install rolls back with CBS_E_INSTALLERS_FAILED (0x800f0922)

steps.action: Search CBS.log for 'Failed to process advanced operation queue' with HRESULT 0x800f0922
steps.expect: Confirms an advanced installer failure triggered the rollback

steps.action: Check C:\Windows\system32\spp\tokens\skus\<edition>\ for 0 KB token files
steps.expect: Compared against a healthy machine, invalid zero-byte files are identified

steps.action: Delete the invalid 0KB token files
steps.expect: Folder now matches the healthy reference machine

steps.action: Reattempt the patch installation
steps.expect: Patch installs successfully without rollback

pending_reboot_blocking_servicing.title: Device is stuck in a pending-reboot state and won't take new updates

steps.action: Run 'Get-PendingReboot' (or check for C:\Windows\WinSXS\pending.xml)
steps.expect: Identifies which category is pending: CBServicing, WindowsUpdate, PendFileRename, or PendComputerRename

steps.action: For CBServicing, run 'DISM /online /get-packages' and check for a package stuck in a pending state
steps.expect: A specific incorrectly-staged package is identified, if present

steps.action: Boot to WinRE and run 'Dism /image:C:\ /cleanup-image /revertpendingactions'
steps.expect: Pending CBS actions are reverted cleanly

steps.action: For a stuck WindowsUpdate reboot flag, back up and delete the RebootRequired value under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Auto Update
steps.expect: Reboot-pending flag clears

steps.action: Re-run 'Get-PendingReboot'
steps.expect: Reports no reboot pending; new updates can now be installed

cbs_transaction_workflow_triage.title: Using the CBS.log transaction workflow to localize a servicing failure

steps.action: Search CBS.log for 'Entering stage: Planning' for the failing package (e.g. Package_for_KBxxxxxxx)
steps.expect: Confirms the transaction started and shows package applicability evaluation

steps.action: Step through each stage in order — Resolving (dependency/pin deployment), Staging (payload copy), Install/Uninstall (execute chain)
steps.expect: Identifies the exact stage where the log stops progressing or reports failure

steps.action: If the package reaches Completion but a driver bundle is involved, check the DOQ Staging and Install blocks, then the Critical Driver installation block
steps.expect: Confirms whether a driver install, not the main package, is the actual point of failure

steps.action: Address the specific failure at the identified stage (e.g. a resolve-time dependency conflict, a staging copy error, or a driver INF failure)
steps.expect: The blocking condition at that specific stage is resolved

steps.action: Retry the update and confirm CBS.log reaches 'FinalCommitPackagesState: Started persisting state of packages' and, if applicable, 'End executing advanced installer ... Completion status: S_OK'
steps.expect: Transaction completes cleanly through to reboot-required or full completion

role_feature_install_fails_winrm_plugin_.title: Server role/feature install fails — WinRM plugin corrupt or missing

steps.action: Attempt the role/feature install via Server Manager and confirm the failure references the WinRM plug-in
steps.expect: Confirms the message 'The Server Manager WinRM plug-in might be corrupt or missing'

steps.action: Run the System Update Readiness Tool (CheckSUR) for this OS version if not already run
steps.expect: Checksur.log identifies any underlying component-store corruption contributing to the failure

steps.action: Resolve any 'Unavailable repair files' entries from checksur.log, then run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'
steps.expect: Component store repair completes cleanly

steps.action: Retry installing the role/feature through Server Manager or 'Install-WindowsFeature'
steps.expect: Role/feature installs successfully

steps.action: Confirm the role/feature shows as Installed in Server Manager
steps.expect: No further WinRM plug-in errors on retry

update_stuck_at_percentage_no_error.title: Update progress bar is stuck at a fixed percentage with no error shown

steps.action: Confirm the percentage hasn't moved for at least 30–60 minutes and the disk/CPU are actually idle (not just a slow install)
steps.expect: Confirms a genuine stall rather than a large, still-progressing install

steps.action: Check Task Manager for TiWorker.exe or TrustedInstaller.exe CPU/disk activity, and check CBS.log for the last logged operation
steps.expect: Shows whether work is still happening quietly or has genuinely frozen

steps.action: If genuinely frozen, let it run at least 2+ hours before intervening; if still stuck, hard-restart and let Windows attempt automatic rollback, then retry after clearing SoftwareDistribution/catroot2
steps.expect: Device recovers to a stable state, either completing or cleanly rolling back

steps.action: Retry the update after the cleanup
steps.expect: Update installs and completes without re-hanging at the same percentage

client_not_detecting_update_from_wsus_sc.title: Client doesn't see or download an update approved in WSUS/SCCM

steps.action: Confirm the update is approved for the correct target group in the WSUS/SCCM console and the client is a member of that group
steps.expect: Approval and group targeting are correct

steps.action: Check WindowsUpdate.log (via Get-WindowsUpdateLog) for the client's last scan against the WSUS/SCCM server and any reported errors
steps.expect: Identifies whether the client is even reaching the server, and with what result

steps.action: Force a rescan with 'wuauclt /resetauthorization /detectnow' (or trigger a Machine Policy + Software Updates Scan Cycle in SCCM), and confirm content is reachable from the distribution point/WSUS server
steps.expect: Client re-scans and picks up the approved update

steps.action: Check Update history / compliance state after the next scan
steps.expect: Update shows as installed and compliant
